y1-cell-biology: Both establish cellular and molecular foundations; UCR also introduces genetics, signalling and physiology.
y2-cellular-biochemistry: Both directly study cellular molecular mechanisms and biochemical processes; the external course remains specifically pharmaceutical in context.
y1-physiology-histology: Both study human physiological systems; UCR does not reproduce the external histology component.
y1-biochemistry: Both directly study biomolecule chemistry and metabolism; UCR does not provide the external organic-chemistry sequence.
y1-biochemistry-lab: Both practise DNA isolation and analysis, bacterial transformation, protein purification and biochemical laboratory reporting. UCR does not reproduce the entire pharmaceutical laboratory sequence.
y1-molecular-genetics: Both directly address molecular genetics; UCR integrates genetics with pathology and treatment.
y2-anatomy: Both directly study human anatomy; UCR emphasises structure/function and imaging rather than the full external biomedical sequence.
y1-pkpd: Both directly study pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, drug targets, dose-response and toxicity.
y2-immunology: Both directly study immune mechanisms; UCR additionally emphasises infection and immunopathology.
y2-pathology: Both directly study disease mechanisms and organ-system pathology.
y2-machine-learning: Both develop machine-learning methods; UCR supplies a general data-science course rather than pharmaceutical applications.
y1-mathematics: Both provide mathematical foundations for pharmaceutical and biomedical science; UCR focuses on calculus and differential equations.
y1-statistics: Both develop probability, random variables and statistical inference including estimation and hypothesis tests. Leiden also teaches practical R data preparation, visualisation and biomedical analysis; UCR emphasises mathematical foundations and sampling algorithms.
y2-statistics: Both develop statistical analysis of biomedical or human data; UCR emphasises multivariate and experimental methods.
y1-academic-skills: Both support academic development; UCR PPD also includes personal, civic and collaborative formation.
y3-modern-drug-development: Both teach study design, bias, confounding, risk measures and appraisal of intervention evidence. These are a substantial assessed pharmacoepidemiology strand in Leiden’s course; UCR does not reproduce its drug-development dossier, clinical phases, regulation or commercialisation.

audience.programmeDescription: Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences studies how medicines are discovered, designed, analysed, delivered and evaluated. Leiden combines chemistry, molecular and medical biology, quantitative methods and practical drug research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme emphasises molecular mechanisms, drug action, disease and biomedical research. The second gives greater weight to mathematical modelling and computational prediction. Both support a substantial part of the biological and quantitative study of medicines, while Leiden provides the specialist chemistry, synthesis, pharmaceutical analysis, formulation and integrated drug-development training.

curriculum.limitation: The ordinary programme totals 180 EC: 60 EC in each of the first two years, then 14 EC of compulsory study, 16 EC of research and 30 EC of approved open study. The selective Pharmacy direction and specific elective packages are optional. The research assignment is continuous and cannot be combined with other courses or practicals.

componentNotes.y3-open-elective-space: 30 EC of open study in the first semester of year three. A Leiden, Delft or Rotterdam minor or a standard approved package is permitted. Self-composed packages, other-institution minors and later changes require prior examination-board approval.
componentNotes.y3-research-practical: Required parts of one continuous ten-week research assignment, normally starting in April after the first-semester open space and the earlier spring teaching. First-year completion and passed second-year practical units are required; one outstanding practical may restrict available placements. Timely questionnaire and academic statement are required. The assignment may produce a research article or an extensive research proposal. Practical work, written report and oral presentation must each pass at 6.0 or higher. Other courses or practicals cannot run alongside the assignment; at most two half-days are allowed for other teaching or a resit. Extending the assignment adds no EC.
componentNotes.y3-research-thesis: Required 3-EC written report within the 16-EC research assignment. The report can be a scientific article or an extensive research proposal; this is not an additional project.
componentNotes.y3-research-presentation: Required 1-EC English presentation of the research or research proposal, within the same 16-EC assignment.
componentNotes.y3-modern-drug-development: Required 13-EC study of the development process, clinical phases, regulation, commercialisation and post-marketing evaluation, including a simulated drug dossier and a substantial pharmacoepidemiology strand.
